title.narrative: "Assistance for Collective Centers and Essential Support Services" (ACCESS)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ACCESS project is the strategic successor to the Emergency Assistance and Support to Evacuation (EASE 1.0) initiative, which was successfully funded through the UHF/CBPF. ACCESS builds directly upon the robust operational capacity, established partnership networks, and operational systems created under EASE. Crucially, the implementation of EASE significantly strengthened our operational presence and network capacity within key reception areas, most notably the Lviv target oblast, providing a solid foundation for this next phase.ltbrgtACCESS represents a strategic pivot from purely emergency transit support to focusing on durable solutions, enhanced localization, and deep inclusion. The ultimate aim is to improve the IDP settling process by ensuring safe, accessible accommodation and providing comprehensive, localized protection services where they are needed most.ltbrgtThe comprehensive approach is executed through four inter-related pillars:ltbrgtStrengthening Local Capacity:ltbrgtWe extend the localization priority of our previous work by directly supporting local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), National Non-Governmental Organizations (NNGOs), and prioritizing Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs). This support includes a structured program of grants, focused mentoring, and specialized training on protection, PSEA, and disability inclusion. This strategy ensures that high-quality protection and case management services are integrated into local civil society structures, guaranteeing service continuity and increasing the long-term sustainability and resilience of the local response ecosystem.ltbrgtInclusive Infrastructure and Dignified Settling:ltbrgtA core component of ACCESS is financing the repairs and strategic upgrades of IDP collective sites. This activity is explicitly designed to address critical barriers to access and inclusion faced by priority groups: elderly IDPs and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). All repairs strictly adhere to national accessibility standards, ensuring that facilities offer dignified, safe, and accessible accommodation and reduce the isolation of the most vulnerable residents.ltbrgtSpecialized Protection Services and Case Management:ltbrgtThe project delivers targeted and critical protection activities and case management services through both static and mobile teams. These specialized services are available for vulnerable IDPs both within the improved collective sites and in broader surrounding host communities. Services include legal counseling, psychosocial support (PSS) referrals, and individual protection assistance, all managed through a sensitive case management protocol designed to address the complex and evolving needs of displaced individuals.ltbrgtGovernance, Coordination, and Accountability:ltbrgtWe ensure institutional sustainability and alignment by providing targeted training to local authorities and collective site management on protection approaches, disability inclusion, and PSEA. The project operates within a Consortium structure to ensure efficient resource sharing and joint learning. Furthermore, ACCESS maintains a robust, proven Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) mechanism, utilizing accessible feedback channels and maintaining close, active coordination with the Protection and CCCM Clusters to prevent duplication and maximize coverage.ltbrgtThis project ensures the most vulnerable IDPs receive tailored support that bridges the gap between emergency crisis and stable, inclusive living conditions through highly localized and strategically coordinated efforts.lt/pgt
